turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Hello! Let me solve one example and explain.
You eat dinner at eight. My grandfather eats dinner at eight.
Why -s? "My grandfather" is one man, so he is "he". After he, she or it, the verb adds -s.
Rule: after he, she or it, add -s or -es to the verb.
Right: The cat sleeps all day. Wrong: The cat sleep all day.

Your turn now. Write only the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
